summary: A fixed three-point metric admits valid fractional solutions with arbitrarily small positive service radii. The printed potential then violates both its terminal bound and core one-step amortized inequality. Zero radii also make the potentials undefined. This is a demonstrated core proof failure, not a counterexample to actual recourse competitiveness.
limitations: No repository acquired/located in checked sources; release status unknown.
Original positive-body-chasing paper not independently re-proved; used only as restated.
No complete repaired amortization, false actual recourse theorem, or empirical reproduction established.
Lower-bound parameter/multiplicity scope and experiment implementation unresolved.
